native_notes.text:
As a reminder, do your workout comments going forward like this:

1. Workout Readiness - (e.g. 6/10; couldn't fall asleep bc of stress)
2. Workout Execution - (e.g. 5/10; skipped last set after going too hard in the first set)
3. Nutrition - (e.g. 5/10; didn't eat during my hard 2 hour interval ride, but did eat before and after)
4. Misc - (e.g. lower back acting up again)

1-3: Rate out of 10 (10 is the best); add details if possible; e.g., "I ate two 50g carbohydrate bars" or "Felt sluggish to start" etc.
Misc: Have at it, or don't.
native_notes.title: How To Comment On Workouts

native_notes.text:
Week 1 of 4. Base. Nothing flashy; I want steady work and the point is accumulation.

This block: Getting the calendar back to something you can actually hit. I care about frequency and rhythm first, duration second, and nothing else until January.

Endurance — Cadence Focus Sunday: power stays flat, the gear changes. Low rungs load the legs, high rungs teach them to spin. Watch the knees on the low stuff.

Watch the easy days. If they creep up in pace, the hard days will start falling short.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Base

native_notes.text: Legs heavy today is the load landing, not a warning sign.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Midweek

native_notes.text:
Tell me:
1. What went well and why?
2. What went badly and why?
3. ONE thing you can DO next week that's:
 a) In your control
 b) Not too big of a lift
 c) Impactful

Please complete this at the end of every week and put your answers in the comments on this note. It will greatly improve you as an athlete and help me coach you better.
native_notes.title: Week Self Review - 3 Qs

native_notes.text:
Week 2 of 4. Base, still. The same shape as last week with a little more in it. That is how base works.

Ronnestad 30-15 Thursday. The short recoveries are the trick: you never fully recover, so the oxygen system stays pinned without the legs blowing up.

The fitness is in the weeks you don't notice.

Sleep is the variable you control. Seven hours minimum this week, more after the hard days.
native_notes.title: Week 2: Base

native_notes.text: If today feels flat, that is the last two hard days still in your legs. Normal.
native_notes.title: Week 2: Midweek

native_notes.text:
Tell me:
1. What went well and why?
2. What went badly and why?
3. ONE thing you can DO next week that's:

Please complete this at the end of every week and put your answers in the comments on this note. It will greatly improve you as an athlete and help me coach you better.
native_notes.title: Week Self Review - 3 Qs

native_notes.text:
Week 3 of 4. Last load week of this block. I want the key sessions done properly; a reset follows.

Ronnestad 30-15 Thursday is the hardest thing this week. Start the first rep at the number, not above it, and let the set get hard on its own.

Missed work stays missed. Do not stack two hard days to make up a session.
native_notes.title: Week 3: Base

native_notes.text: A dead-legs day mid-week is the training working, not the training gone wrong.
native_notes.title: Week 3: Midweek

2. What went badly and why?
3. ONE thing you can DO next week that's:

Please complete this at the end of every week and put your answers in the comments on this note. It will greatly improve you as an athlete and help me coach you better.
native_notes.title: Week Self Review - 3 Qs

native_notes.text:
Week 4 of 4. Recovery week, and I mean it: the last block gets absorbed now, not later.

Tune-Up Thursday: short, sharp, and done before you feel like you have started. The point is to wake the legs, not test them.

Fatigue should drop noticeably by Thursday. If it does not, say so before the weekend.

workouts.description:
WARM-UP:
- 9min building from Z1 into the Z2 target

MAIN SET:
- 43min @ 68% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- Position: Alternate every 30 min: drops (aero) → hoods (power)
- Cadence: self-selected, comfortable endurance cadence

COOL-DOWN:
- 9min easy spin Z1-Z2 (RPE 3-4)
workouts.title: Endurance — Position Focus

workouts.description:
Off the bike, not off the plan.

Ten minutes of hip and lower-back mobility, the stuff that gets skipped on ride days. A 20-30 minute walk if the legs feel like wood. Lights out thirty minutes earlier than usual.

No riding. Tomorrow needs you.
workouts.title: Rest Day

workouts.description:
Off the bike. This week's work gets absorbed today, not added to.

Foam roll quads and glutes, eight to ten minutes. One long walk. Eat like you trained; a rest day is not a diet day.

If you feel great and want to ride, that is the point. Don't.
workouts.title: Rest Day

workouts.description:
WARM-UP:
- 9min building from Z1 into the Z2 target

MAIN SET:
- 44min @ 68% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- Drill: 30sec spin-up @ 100-110rpm every 10min — no extra power, just leg speed
- Position: Stay relaxed on the hoods; keep shoulders quiet
- Cadence: Every 10 min, spin 30 sec at 100-110rpm, then settle smoothly

COOL-DOWN:
- 9min easy spin Z1-Z2 (RPE 3-4)

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Normal meal ~2h before. One bottle, 40-50g carbs. Done.

WARM-UP:
-12min ramp Z1->Z2, then 2x1min @113% with 1min easy

MAIN SET:
-3 sets of 11x (30s @110% FTP / 15s @50%)
-3min @50% between sets
-Cadence: 90-110rpm, seated and smooth

EXECUTION:
-Hit target on every 30s. The float is a true easy spin. End a set if you can't hold the 30s power in its back third.

NUTRITION:
-30-60g carbs/hr.

HYDRATION:
-500-750ml/hr with electrolytes.

RPE guide: 113% FTP -> RPE 8-9; 110% FTP -> RPE 8-9; 50% FTP -> RPE 3
workouts.pre_activity_comment:
Feels great? Extend the duration at the same power -- never add power.
Failed a set? Resume after 5-10min easy only if the early reps weren't already a struggle. Struggling from rep one: spin home easy and tell me.

Recovery-week rest day. Fatigue is supposed to drop this week; help it.

Ten minutes of mobility, a nap if you can get one, an honest early bedtime. Eat enough. A recovery week is not a weight-loss week.

Feeling flat today is normal. Still flat on Friday, message me.
workouts.title: Rest Day

workouts.description:
Reset day. The block lands now.

A walk, a stretch, food on the plate. Nothing with a heart-rate strap.

If you are itching to ride, good. Hold it. That itch is the fitness arriving.
workouts.title: Rest Day

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Normal meal ~2h before. One bottle, 40-50g carbs. Done.

MAIN SET:
- 24min @ 65% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 2 x (0:18 @ 140% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9) + 2:30 @ 55% FTP (Z2, RPE 3))
- 0:18 @ 140% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9)
- 5min @ 50% FTP (Z1, RPE 3)
-Cadence: 95-105rpm on efforts
-Position: Seated, relaxed

PROGRESSION:
-Level 1/6: Introductory - Focus on form and learning the workout pattern
-Short alactic openers -- three brief near-max efforts to wake up neuromuscular firing without creating fatigue

EXECUTION:
-Short sharp efforts to keep the legs remembering speed. Don't dig deep - this should feel like play, not training.
